source.original_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
There exists rho:Prefix_n(T)->Prefix_n(T) with (rho t)_i=T-t_(n-1-i) for every i. It is Borel measurable, involutive, and preserves m_n,T. For all y,r,z,t, the terminal identity is A_(y,r)(z,t)=Phi_(y,r,T-q_n)(z_n). The map (y,r,z,t)->A_(y,r)(z,t) is jointly Borel measurable. For each y,r,t, z->A_(y,r)(z,t) preserves ell. The reversed endpoint satisfies A_(y,r)(R(A_(y,r)(z,t)),rho t)=R(z).
Define Theta_(y,r)(z,t)=(R(A_(y,r)(z,t)),rho t). The map (y,r,z,t)->Theta_(y,r)(z,t) is jointly Borel measurable. For each y,r, Theta_(y,r) is an involution and preserves ell tensor m_n,T, in phase-first order. Every measure-preservation assertion includes measurability and equality of pushforward measures. All conclusions include n=0, T=0, zero reflection normals and rank-zero E; measurability, inverses, sigma finiteness and volume identities are proved internally from the six analytic assumptions.
This is the finite prescribed endpoint/time change of variables used in the Appendix A.1 reversal argument. It does not assert pointwise time reversal of right-continuous paths at event times. Gibbs-weight balance, stationary averaging and invariant probability laws, Markov properties, hypocoercivity, implementation error, expected oracle costs, main sampling results and actual-input composition remain separate obligations.

    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) : by
  classical
  exact
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}

    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)

    let R : (E × E) → (E × E) := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let ell : Measure (E × E) := (volume : Measure E).prod (volume : Measure E)

          (zAt y r z n T t (Fin.last n))) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        A p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 p.2) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
        MeasurePreserving (fun z => A y r z t) ell ell) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
        A y r (R (A y r z t)) (rho t) = R z) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        Theta p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 (p.1.2, p.2)) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, Function.Involutive (Theta y r)) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, MeasurePreserving (Theta y r) (ell.prod (m n T)) (ell.prod (m n T)))
decoder_context: The real Hilbert gradient and Frechet derivative are gradient and fderiv. All measurable spaces on the ambient finite-dimensional real inner-product space are its Borel structure.

volume is canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure. Measure.prod is product measure. Measure.comap under a measurable subtype inclusion gives the subtype measure. MeasurePreserving includes measurability and equality of pushforward measures.

Fin n indexes n coordinates from zero. Fin.cons prepends a coordinate. Fin.rev reverses the index order. Fin.induction is recursion on this finite index, and Fin.foldl applies updates in increasing index order.

Real division by zero equals zero. Real.toNNReal is the nonnegative part. Subtraction in the nonnegative reals is truncated at zero. Sum.inl is the live-record constructor; the other summand has one cemetery value.

A function-valued path has the product measurable structure, and its argument subtype is the closed interval from zero to the displayed horizon. Function.Involutive means composing the map with itself gives the identity. The zero-coordinate tuple is unique.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualFiniteCountPath

import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Rev
import Mathlib.Order.Fin.Tuple

/-! Actual finite prescribed endpoint and time-tuple reversal for PBPS A.8.
Original six analytic assumptions; phase volume and ordered-simplex comap volume.
The right-continuous path itself is not asserted to reverse pointwise at events.
Gibbs density balance, stationary averaging, restart, and full invariance remain separate.
-/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualEndpointTimeReversal
open MeasureTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped NNReal ENNReal Classical ContDiff
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxHeartbeats 2400000


private def delta (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < T}
private def reverseTime {n : ℕ} (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun i => T - t i.rev

private theorem reverseTime_involutive (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    Function.Involutive (reverseTime (n := n) T) := by
  intro t; funext i
  simp [reverseTime]

private theorem reverseTime_mem {n : ℕ} {T : ℝ} {t : Fin n → ℝ}
    (ht : t ∈ delta n T) : reverseTime T t ∈ delta n T := by
  obtain ⟨hpos, hmono⟩ := Fin.strictMono_cons.mp ht.1
  refine ⟨Fin.strictMono_cons.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    exact sub_pos.mpr (ht.2 i.rev)
  · intro i j hij
    exact sub_lt_sub_left (hmono (Fin.rev_lt_rev.mpr hij)) T
  · intro i
    exact sub_lt_self T (hpos i.rev)

private theorem reverseTime_measurable (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    Measurable (reverseTime (n := n) T) := by
  apply measurable_pi_lambda
  intro i
  exact measurable_const.sub (measurable_pi_apply i.rev)

private theorem reverseTime_volume (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    MeasurePreserving (reverseTime (n := n) T) volume volume := by
  have hp := volume_measurePreserving_piCongrLeft (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ) Fin.revPerm

/-- Cancellation of a finite word against its reverse under a common reversing map. -/
private theorem reverse_fold_cancel {X : Type*} (C : X → X) (n : ℕ)
    (f : Fin n → X → X) (hf : ∀ i x, f i (C (f i x)) = C x) (x : X) :
    Fin.foldr n f (C (Fin.foldl n (fun z i => f i z) x)) = C x := by
  induction n generalizing x with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Fin.foldl_succ, Fin.foldr_succ]
    rw [ih (fun i => f i.succ) (fun i => hf i.succ)]
    exact hf 0 x

/-- Finite recursion is the corresponding left fold, without assuming an endpoint. -/
private theorem fold_of_sequence {X : Type*} (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → X → X)
    (r : Fin (n + 1) → X) (x : X) (hzero : r 0 = x)
    (hstep : ∀ i : Fin n, r i.succ = f i (r i.castSucc)) :
    Fin.foldl n (fun z i => f i z) x = r (Fin.last n) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa using hzero.symm
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Fin.foldl_succ_last]
    have ht := ih (fun i => f i.castSucc) (fun i => r i.castSucc) hzero
      (fun i => hstep i.castSucc)
    rw [ht]
    exact (hstep (Fin.last n)).symm

private def gaps {n : ℕ} (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : ℝ :=
  (Fin.snoc t T : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i

private theorem gaps_reversed (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    gaps T (fun j => T - t j.rev) i = gaps T t i.rev := by
  have hl : (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (fun j : Fin n => T - t j.rev) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i = T - (Fin.snoc t T : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.rev := by
    induction i using Fin.cases with
    | zero => simp
    | succ j => simp [Fin.rev_succ]
  have hr : (Fin.snoc (fun j : Fin n => T - t j.rev) T : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i = T - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.rev := by
    induction i using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => simp
    | cast j => simp [Fin.rev_castSucc]
  unfold gaps
  rw [hl, hr]
  ring

private def post {X : Type*} (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S : X → X) (n : ℕ)
    (t : Fin n → ℝ) (z : X) : Fin (n + 1) → X :=
  Fin.induction z (fun i x => S (Φ (t i -
    (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) x))

private def endpoint {X : Type*} (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S : X → X) (n : ℕ)
    (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (z : X) : X :=
  Φ (T - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n))
    (post Φ S n t z (Fin.last n))

private theorem endpoint_as_word {X : Type*} (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S : X → X)
    (hS : Function.Involutive S) (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (z : X) :
    endpoint Φ S n T t z =
      Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun x i => Φ (gaps T t i) (S x)) (S z) := by
  have hSS (x : X) : S (S x) = x := hS x
  let r : Fin (n + 2) → X := Fin.snoc (fun i => S (post Φ S n t z i))
    (endpoint Φ S n T t z)
  have hzero : r 0 = S z := by
    change S (post Φ S n t z 0) = S z
    rfl
  have hstep (i : Fin (n + 1)) : r i.succ = Φ (gaps T t i) (S (r i.castSucc)) := by
    induction i using Fin.lastCases with
    | last =>
      simp only [r, Fin.succ_last, Fin.snoc_last, Fin.snoc_castSucc, endpoint, gaps, hSS]
    | cast j =>
      simp only [r, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, post, Fin.induction_succ, gaps, hSS]
  have hf := fold_of_sequence (n + 1) (fun i x => Φ (gaps T t i) (S x)) r (S z) hzero hstep
  simpa only [r, Fin.snoc_last] using hf.symm

private theorem endpoint_reversed {X : Type*} (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S R : X → X)
    (hS : Function.Involutive S) (hR : Function.Involutive R)
    (hRS : ∀ x, R (S x) = S (R x))
    (hInv : ∀ u x, Φ u (Φ (-u) x) = x)
    (hRev : ∀ u x, R (Φ u (R x)) = Φ (-u) x)
    (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (z : X) :
    endpoint Φ S n T (fun i => T - t i.rev) (R (endpoint Φ S n T t z)) = R z := by
  have hSS (x : X) : S (S x) = x := hS x
  have hRR (x : X) : R (R x) = x := hR x
  have hcomm (u : ℝ) (x : X) : R (Φ u x) = Φ (-u) (R x) := by
    simpa only [hRR] using hRev u (R x)
  let C : X → X := fun x => S (R x)
  let f : Fin (n + 1) → X → X := fun i x => Φ (gaps T t i) (S x)
  have hf (i : Fin (n + 1)) (x : X) : f i (C (f i x)) = C x := by
    dsimp [f, C]
    rw [hSS, hcomm, hInv, hRS]
  rw [endpoint_as_word Φ S hS]
  simp_rw [gaps_reversed]
  change Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun x i => f i.rev x) (C (endpoint Φ S n T t z)) = R z
  rw [Fin.foldl_rev, endpoint_as_word Φ S hS]
  exact (reverse_fold_cancel C (n + 1) f hf (S z)).trans (by dsimp [C]; rw [hRS, hSS])

private theorem preserving_fold {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X)
    (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → X → X) (hf : ∀ i, MeasurePreserving (f i) μ μ) :
    MeasurePreserving (fun x => Fin.foldl n (fun z i => f i z) x) μ μ := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    simp only [Fin.foldl_zero]
    exact ⟨measurable_id, Measure.map_id'⟩
  | succ n ih =>
    simpa only [Fin.foldl_succ_last, Function.comp_def] using
      (hf (Fin.last n)).comp (ih (fun i => f i.castSucc) (fun i => hf i.castSucc))

private theorem endpoint_volume {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X)
    (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S : X → X) (hS : Function.Involutive S)
    (hSM : MeasurePreserving S μ μ) (hΦ : ∀ u, MeasurePreserving (Φ u) μ μ)
    (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) : MeasurePreserving (endpoint Φ S n T t) μ μ := by
  have he : endpoint Φ S n T t =
      (fun x => Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z i => Φ (gaps T t i) (S z)) x) ∘ S := by
    funext z
    exact endpoint_as_word Φ S hS n T t z
  rw [he]
  exact (preserving_fold μ (n + 1) (fun i z => Φ (gaps T t i) (S z))
    (fun i => (hΦ _).comp hSM)).comp hSM

      Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
    Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
      S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
  let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →

    Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)

    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∃ rho : Prefix n T → Prefix n T,

      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>

      (∀ y r : E, Function.Involutive (Theta y r)) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, MeasurePreserving (Theta y r) (ell.prod (m n T)) (ell.prod (m n T)))

  have hAm : Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
      A p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 p.2) := (hed n T).2.2.1
  have hAid (y r : E) (z : E × E) (t : Prefix n T) :
      A y r z t = endpoint (Φ y r) (S r) n (T : ℝ) t.val z := (hed n T).2.2.2 y r z t
  have hAP (y r : E) (t : Prefix n T) : MeasurePreserving (fun z => A y r z t) ell ell := by
    have he : (fun z => A y r z t) = endpoint (Φ y r) (S r) n (T : ℝ) t.val := funext (fun z => hAid y r z t)
    rw [he]

  have hAI (y r : E) (z : E × E) (t : Prefix n T) :
      A y r (R (A y r z t)) (rho₀ t) = R z := by
    rw [hAid, hAid]
    exact endpoint_reversed (Φ y r) (S r) R (hSI r) hRI (hRS r)
      (fun u z => (hΦI y r u z).2) (hRΦ y r) n (T : ℝ) t.val z

      Theta p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 (p.1.2, p.2)) :=
    (hRP.measurable.comp hAm).prodMk (hrM.comp measurable_snd)
  refine ⟨(hed n T).2.2.2, hAm, hAP, hAI, hThetaM, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro y r q
    apply Prod.ext
    · change R (A y r (R (A y r q.1 q.2)) (rho₀ q.2)) = q.1
      rw [hAI]
      exact hRI q.1
    · exact hrI q.2

    have hs := (hed n T).1

      change SigmaFinite ((Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val)
        (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))).map (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val))
      rw [map_comap_subtype_coe hs]
      infer_instance
    letI : SigmaFinite (m n T) := SigmaFinite.of_map (m n T) measurable_subtype_coe.aemeasurable hmσ

For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.

Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. steps.text: Set rho(t)_i=T-t_(n-1-i). Reversal reverses index order and subtraction reverses inequalities, so strict ordering is preserved. The original upper bound gives positivity, and the original positivity gives the new upper bound T. Applying the formula twice restores every coordinate. private def delta (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < T}
private def reverseTime {n : ℕ} (T : ℝ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun i => T - t i.rev

private theorem reverseTime_involutive (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    Function.Involutive (reverseTime (n := n) T) := by
  intro t; funext i
  simp [reverseTime]

private theorem reverseTime_mem {n : ℕ} {T : ℝ} {t : Fin n → ℝ}
    (ht : t ∈ delta n T) : reverseTime T t ∈ delta n T := by
  obtain ⟨hpos, hmono⟩ := Fin.strictMono_cons.mp ht.1
  refine ⟨Fin.strictMono_cons.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    exact sub_pos.mpr (ht.2 i.rev)
  · intro i j hij
    exact sub_lt_sub_left (hmono (Fin.rev_lt_rev.mpr hij)) T
  · intro i
    exact sub_lt_self T (hpos i.rev)

private theorem reverseTime_measurable (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    Measurable (reverseTime (n := n) T) := by
  apply measurable_pi_lambda
  intro i
  exact measurable_const.sub (measurable_pi_apply i.rev)

private theorem reverseTime_volume (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    MeasurePreserving (reverseTime (n := n) T) volume volume := by
  have hp := volume_measurePreserving_piCongrLeft (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ) Fin.revPerm
  have heq : (fun t : Fin n → ℝ => fun i : Fin n => t i.rev) =
      MeasurableEquiv.piCongrLeft (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ) Fin.revPerm := by
    funext t i
    symm
    simpa only [Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.rev_rev] using
      (MeasurableEquiv.piCongrLeft_apply_apply (β := fun _ : Fin n => ℝ) Fin.revPerm t i.rev)
  rw [← heq] at hp
  have hc : MeasurePreserving (fun t : Fin n → ℝ => fun i => T - t i) volume volume :=

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
There exists rho:Prefix_n(T)->Prefix_n(T) with (rho t)_i=T-t_(n-1-i) for every i. It is Borel measurable, involutive, and preserves m_n,T. For all y,r,z,t, the terminal identity is A_(y,r)(z,t)=Phi_(y,r,T-q_n)(z_n). The map (y,r,z,t)->A_(y,r)(z,t) is jointly Borel measurable. For each y,r,t, z->A_(y,r)(z,t) preserves ell. The reversed endpoint satisfies A_(y,r)(R(A_(y,r)(z,t)),rho t)=R(z).
Define Theta_(y,r)(z,t)=(R(A_(y,r)(z,t)),rho t). The map (y,r,z,t)->Theta_(y,r)(z,t) is jointly Borel measurable. For each y,r, Theta_(y,r) is an involution and preserves ell tensor m_n,T, in phase-first order. Every measure-preservation assertion includes measurability and equality of pushforward measures. All conclusions include n=0, T=0, zero reflection normals and rank-zero E; measurability, inverses, sigma finiteness and volume identities are proved internally from the six analytic assumptions.
This is the finite prescribed endpoint/time change of variables used in the Appendix A.1 reversal argument. It does not assert pointwise time reversal of right-continuous paths at event times. Gibbs-weight balance, stationary averaging and invariant probability laws, Markov properties, hypocoercivity, implementation error, expected oracle costs, main sampling results and actual-input composition remain separate obligations.

# Independent mathematical reconstruction

This reconstruction uses only the anonymous Lean statement and approved definition context in the supplied input packet. It makes no source-comparison verdict. The input reports compilation; this decoder did not independently run Lean or inspect a proof.

## Ambient objects and hypotheses

Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its induced norm and Borel measurable structure. No positive-dimension or nontriviality hypothesis is imposed. Let V : E → ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α, β be nonnegative real numbers, and let η be real. Assume

- α > 0 and α ≤ β;
- for every x, v ∈ E, α ‖v‖² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ β ‖v‖²;
- η > 0 and βη ≤ 1.

Here D²V(x)[v,v] is precisely (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v, and ∇V is the real Hilbert-space gradient. The Hessian bounds hold globally for every x and v. All statements below are under these fixed hypotheses. In particular β > 0 and √η > 0. No normalization of exp(-V), stochastic law, probability density, or initial-state distribution is assumed.

## Explicit definitions

For arbitrary y, r ∈ E put c = y − η∇V(r). On the phase space E × E, define for every real s

Φ(y,r,s,(x,v)) = (c + cos(s)(x−c) + √η sin(s)v,
                    −sin(s)/√η (x−c) + cos(s)v).

Scalar multiplication of vectors is understood in this formula. In particular the displayed trigonometric argument is s itself. For g_r(x) = ∇V(x) − ∇V(r), define

S(r,(x,v)) = (x, v − [2⟨v,g_r(x)⟩/‖g_r(x)‖²]g_r(x)).

The inner product is real. Real division by zero is defined as zero. Thus S fixes (x,v) whenever g_r(x)=0; the statement does not require this gradient difference to be nonzero.

For each integer n ≥ 0 and nonnegative real horizon T, let P(n,T) be the subtype of n real coordinates t = (t₁,…,tₙ) satisfying

0 < t₁ < ⋯ < tₙ < T.

Precisely, the Lean coordinates are indexed by Fin n from zero: our tₖ denotes the coordinate with index k−1. The first strict inequality and ordering are expressed by strict monotonicity of the tuple with an initial zero prepended. Put τ₀=0 and τⱼ=tⱼ for 1 ≤ j ≤ n. Let m(n,T) be the pullback, by the subtype inclusion P(n,T) → ℝⁿ, of canonical Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ. Equivalently, it is Lebesgue measure on the open ordered-time simplex, represented on that subtype. It is not normalized to be a probability measure.

For z₀ ∈ E × E and t ∈ P(n,T), define recursively

zⱼ₊₁ = S(r, Φ(y,r,τⱼ₊₁−τⱼ,zⱼ)),  0 ≤ j < n.

Thus zⱼ is the recorded state after the event at τⱼ for j ≥ 1, and z₀ is the initial recorded state. The finite record type is Rec = ([0,∞) × (E × E)) ⊔ {cemetery}, and Hist(n) consists of n+1 records indexed from zero. The canonical history K records the live pair (τⱼ,zⱼ) at every index j=0,…,n. Formally its timestamp is max(τⱼ,0), which equals τⱼ for these admissible tuples.

The path type Path(T) is the set of functions [0,T] → E × E, equipped with its product measurable structure. For an arbitrary history h, Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,h)(s) is defined by the following finite fold in increasing record-index order. Start with accumulator z₀. For each live record (a,w), replace the accumulator by Φ(y,r,s−a,w) if a ≤ s; otherwise leave it unchanged. Cemetery records also leave the accumulator unchanged. The subtraction used formally is truncated nonnegative-real subtraction, then coerced to ℝ; in the branch a ≤ s it is ordinary s−a. For arbitrary histories this selects the last eligible record by index, not necessarily the largest timestamp.

Define Γ(y,r,z₀,n,T,t) = Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)). Since K has increasing timestamps, at each s ∈ [0,T] this path flows from the most recent recorded state zⱼ with τⱼ ≤ s. At an event time it uses the post-event record, with zero elapsed flow. Finally define the terminal-state map

A(y,r,z,t) = Γ(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T),

the velocity reversal R(x,v)=(x,−v), and the phase-volume measure ℓ = vol_E ⊗ vol_E. Dependence of A on the fixed n,T is suppressed in this notation.

## Reconstructed theorem

For every n ≥ 0 and T ≥ 0 there exists a single map ρ : P(n,T) → P(n,T), chosen before and independently of the quantified y,r,z, with all the following properties.

1. For each admissible t and each k=1,…,n,

   (ρ(t))ₖ = T − tₙ₊₁₋ₖ.

   This map is measurable, is an involution (ρ(ρ(t))=t), and preserves the measure m(n,T). Preservation means its pushforward of m(n,T) equals m(n,T); the Lean MeasurePreserving predicate also includes measurability.

2. For every y,r ∈ E, every z ∈ E × E, and every t ∈ P(n,T), the terminal state equals the flow after the last recorded event:

   A(y,r,z,t) = Φ(y,r,T−τₙ,zₙ).

   Here the recursion defining zₙ starts at the quantified initial state z, and τₙ is the last entry of (0,t₁,…,tₙ).

3. The map (y,r,z,t) ↦ A(y,r,z,t) is jointly measurable from ((E × E) × (E × E)) × P(n,T) to E × E, with its displayed product/subtype measurable structures. The first E × E packages y,r; the second packages the initial position and velocity. The claim is for each fixed n,T, not a joint measurability claim across n,T or V,α,β,η.

4. For every fixed y,r ∈ E and every fixed t ∈ P(n,T), the map z ↦ A(y,r,z,t) preserves ℓ on E × E, including measurability of this map.

5. For every y,r,z,t as above, terminal evolution with reversed velocity and reflected event times satisfies the exact identity

   A(y,r,R(A(y,r,z,t)),ρ(t)) = R(z).

   The parameters y and r are held fixed in both evolutions.

6. Define the map on phase state and event times

   Θ(y,r,(z,t)) = (R(A(y,r,z,t)),ρ(t)).

   The map (y,r,z,t) ↦ Θ(y,r,(z,t)) is jointly measurable on the same packaged input domain as in item 3, with codomain (E × E) × P(n,T). For every fixed y,r, Θ(y,r,·) is an involution and preserves the product measure ℓ ⊗ m(n,T). Thus applying Θ twice returns exactly (z,t); its measure-preservation assertion is equality of pushforward and original product measure, together with measurability.

All these conclusions hold simultaneously for the same ρ at fixed n,T. There are no existential unspecified constants in the conclusion and no omitted small-time, dimension, initial-state, or reference-point restriction. The constants α,β appear as assumptions; the constructed flow and event reflection use V,η and y,r. The formula for ρ uses only n,T and t. No rates or quantitative probability bounds are asserted.

## Empty, zero, and scope cases

When n=0, P(0,T) contains the unique empty tuple for every T ≥ 0, including T=0. Its measure is the zero-dimensional canonical Lebesgue measure, with mass one on that point. There are no event reflections; zₙ=z and τₙ=0, so A(y,r,z,t)=Φ(y,r,T,z). The map ρ is the identity on the singleton.

When T=0 and n>0, P(n,0) is empty. Its measure is zero, the map ρ is the unique empty-domain map, and all conclusions quantified over admissible event tuples are vacuous; the corresponding phase/time product domain is empty. When n=0 and T=0, A is the identity on phase states and Θ acts by velocity reversal on the phase state and identity on the empty tuple.

Zero-dimensional E is allowed. Phase space is then a singleton and all vector formulas have their usual zero-dimensional meaning. Zero gradient differences are explicitly allowed, with the event map equal to the identity there. The square-root denominators in Φ never divide by zero because η>0.

The path Γ is used through its definition and terminal evaluation. The proposition does not separately assert joint measurability of the entire path-valued Γ, path continuity, a distribution of random event times, invariance of a target probability measure, convergence, or a finite-time error estimate. Measures preserved in the explicit conclusions are Lebesgue phase volume, simplex Lebesgue measure, and their product. No statement about arbitrary histories h beyond the definition of Ψ is part of the conclusion.
